name: Vinayaka Mylari
blurb: A six-table Mysuru institution since the late 1930s, making one soft, ghee-roasted dosa and nothing else worth asking about. Grab a churmuri from the puffed-rice stalls outside Devaraja Market on the way.
try: One soft, ghee-roasted dosa at a six-table Mysuru room that's been doing only that.
Don't ask for a masala stuffed the Bengaluru way.

name: Nandi Hills
blurb: A pre-dawn drive up a hill fort for sunrise above the clouds - a Bengaluru weekend ritual long before Instagram.
try: Leave well before dawn for sunrise above the cloud line.
It's a hill-fort drive, not a cafe with a view - start early or sit in traffic.

name: Mysuru Palace
blurb: Karnataka's own answer to a "royal palace" - Indo-Saracenic architecture, lit up gold every Sunday evening.
try: The palace lit gold on a Sunday evening if you can time it.
Walk the front, then the city market and a Mylari dosa, not only the ticketed rooms.

name: Coorg (Kodagu)
blurb: Misty coffee estates, Kodava culture, and a cuisine (pandi curry, kadambuttu) unlike anything else on this list.
try: Estate coffee, pandi curry, kadambuttu - stay overnight if you can.
This is Kodava country, not a Bengaluru weekend park.

name: Sakleshpur
blurb: Karnataka's coffee country in the Western Ghats, about 220km from Bengaluru - shade-grown Arabica and Robusta estates, pepper vines climbing silver oak, and Manjarabad Fort, a star-shaped hilltop fort Tipu Sultan built in 1792. The old Sakleshpur-Subramanya railway line, threading 57 tunnels and 100-plus bridges, was a famous trek route only while trains weren't running on it - it's since been electrified and returned to active service, so it's a train line again, not a trail.
try: A coffee-estate walk and stay, not just a drive-through - pepper vines, cardamom, and the drying yards in season.
Manjarabad Fort's star-shaped ramparts, 5km out of town - free entry, 8am-6pm.

name: Channapatna
area: ~1.5 hrs south, on the Mysuru road
blurb: The "town of toys" - lacquered wooden toys turned on a lathe, a craft old enough to have a GI tag. Workshops will let you watch.
try: Watch lacquered toys turned on a lathe, then buy from the makers, not a mall shelf.
A stop on the Mysuru road, not a full-day destination unless you linger at a workshop.

name: Babusingh Thakur Peda
blurb: The original Dharwad Peda shop - over 175 years on the same Line Bazaar spot, still run by the same family across multiple generations. The queues for it are reportedly why the street is called Line Bazaar in the first place.
try: Dharwad Peda from the Line Bazaar shop that's been on the same spot 175 years.
Cash, queue, take a box; that's the pilgrimage.

name: Chikmagalur
blurb: Karnataka's coffee country - Western Ghats estates, waterfalls, and the trail up Mullayanagiri, the state's highest peak.
try: An estate walk and the Mullayanagiri trail if you have the legs.
Coffee country - stay a night, don't treat it as a day from Bengaluru unless you must.

name: Udupi & Mangaluru coast
area: ~7 hrs west, or a short flight
blurb: Krishna Matt's temple kitchens, Malpe's beaches, and a coastal cuisine - neer dosa, kori rotti, Mangalorean seafood - worlds from Bengaluru's own. Eat at Mitra Samaj by the temple, where masala dosa was reportedly invented in 1949 - and try the Mangalore bun and goli baje while you're there. Detour up NH66 to Maravanthe, where the road runs on a strip of land with the Arabian Sea on one side and the Souparnika river on the other - a geography not repeated anywhere else in India.
try: Temple-kitchen Udupi food, Malpe beach, neer dosa and kori rotti.
Coastal Karnataka is a trip, not a lunch.

name: Melkote (Melukote)
blurb: A Srivaishnavite pilgrimage town on a rocky hill above Mandya, older than its most famous legend - epigraphic evidence shows the deity was already worshipped here before Ramanuja arrived around 1098 CE and installed it as Tirunarayana. The Vairamudi festival every March/April draws 400,000-plus people to see the deity crowned with the Vairamudi, a diamond crown of unknown donor, alongside two Wodeyar-gifted crowns normally kept under state custody in the Mandya treasury.
try: Climb to the Yoga Narasimha temple on the hilltop - believed installed by Prahlada himself, and the better view.
Time it for Vairamudi habba (March/April) if you want to see all three royal crowns out at once.

name: Yakshagana Kendra
blurb: A training school for Yakshagana, coastal Karnataka's all-night dance-drama - towering headgear, painted faces, a live Bhagavatha narrating epics to drums and cymbals. Ask locally for a mela performance nearby; the season runs roughly November to May.
try: If a performance or rehearsal is on, that's the visit - costumes and all-night drama.
It's a training school in Udupi, not a museum diorama.

name: Hampi
area: ~6-7 hrs north, better as an overnight
blurb: The boulder-strewn ruins of the Vijayanagara empire's capital - temples, market streets, and elephant stables carved into a lunar landscape.
try: Boulder ruins, temple streets, and the river - plan an overnight, not a day dash.
Sunrise or late afternoon; midday on the rocks is punishment.

name: Vijayapura (Bijapur)
blurb: Deccan sultanate architecture at full scale - the Gol Gumbaz dome, second largest in the world, has a whisper gallery worth the echo.
try: Gol Gumbaz first, then the other sultanate buildings if you still have light.
Pair with Hampi or Aihole; it's a long north Karnataka haul.

name: Aihole, Badami & Pattadakal
area: ~9-10 hrs north, pair with Hampi or Vijayapura
blurb: Three Chalukya-era temple towns on the Malaprabha river - the "primary school, secondary school and university" of Indian temple architecture, centuries older than Hampi. Pinned here at Badami, the natural base for touring all three.
try: Aihole, Badami, Pattadakal as one Chalukya chain along the Malaprabha.
Temple-town hopping - start early, one site rushed is a waste.
